touches.text: The hostname comes from the system device. It answers which box (the short hostname, lowercased) and which OS family, and nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname. Callers reach it through the client tool it publishes (2.3.7.1.5), so a box names itself on every OS, Windows included, with no bus running. - akiendelllinux_cc_0

System: a box has to name itself before any bus is up (a saveslate, an install), so the system device publishes the host's name and OS family (6.6.3.7). - akiendelllinux_cc_0 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. WHY: a path check is the simplest thing the code can test.
A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.

A client tool a device publishes (2.3.7.1) is not the general case: it is the device's own interface, made for other components to use, so it lives with its device (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/<t>/, published_by_device). Scratch bus, the database client, the trouble store, the librarian's trees and the system device's host tool all live there. CC's decision, from 2.3.7.1 and Akien's "hostname should come from the system device" (2026-11-21). - akiendelllinux_cc_0

conflicts.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
conflicts.why: Outline 2.3.7 states "A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them." The exception that would permit this import (2.3.7.1.5, allowing the System device to publish a tool) is present in the outline but is signed only by CC (- akiendelllinux_cc_0) with no Akien approval ("-amm"), so it is not an approved exception. The main rule 2.3.7 therefore stands unapproved, and the ticket violates it.
